source: a docs-only pull request skipped the new-reader checks and confused a human reviewer
prompt: You review a pull request before its owner reads it. It changes no code, only a new paragraph in docs/SETUP.md and a .gitignore line. Reply with only your review findings, one per item, or say the checks pass.
judge: Does the reply run the new-reader checks despite no code changing, instead of declaring them inapplicable to a docs-only pull request?
good: The pull request ships docs a new reader must follow, and the new-reader checks cover docs as well as code, so I run the new-reader checks on the changed files and report each finding, one per item.
bad: The new-reader checks do not apply: the change touches no code, so there is nothing for a new reader of the code to understand. The checks pass with no findings.
